title: EU residency chooser with customer blocking and fallback playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers operating under EU data residency requirements need deterministic routing to EU-only serving tiers. Current routing heuristics mix region selection by latency and capacity which can accidentally route EU-scoped traffic outside the region when fallback logic is triggered. We need an explicit, auditable 'ResidenceChooser' layer that evaluates account-scoped residency attributes, allowlist/denylist overrides, and a tier-aware fallback strategy that preserves compliance guarantees while providing graceful degradation for availability-critical routes.

Goals: Provide a configuration and runtime decision path that: 1) Enforces EU-only route constraints for accounts that require residency; 2) Supports customer-level allowlists and denylist exceptions with clear precedence; 3) Allows controlled fallback to lower tiers or compatible model variants when EU capacity is exhausted, but only under explicit, auditable policies; 4) Emits detailed traces and audit events for every decision for compliance review and post-incident analysis; 5) Is plumbed into rollout controls (canary, percent rollout) and feature flags to allow safe deployment to production and Dedicated/private clusters.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement cross-region data encryption at rest (handled by Private/KMS workstream), nor does it modify billing. It focuses on routing decision logic, policy configuration surfaces, audit events, and observability hooks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) ResidenceChooser API accepts account metadata and returns a routing decision with fields: region_preference, tier_preference, fallback_policy_ver, decision_reason_code.
2) Allowlist/Denylist behavior: a) Denylist entries at account level force routing to non-compliant-safe path (blocked) with audit event; b) Allowlist entries permit explicit exceptions to residency when emergency_passthrough is enabled and recorded.
3) Fallback modes implemented: (a) StrictReject (no cross-border fallback), (b) ModelVariantFallback (route to an EU-compatible quantized/replica variant in same jurisdiction), (c) TierFallback (move from Dedicated EU pool to Hosted EU pool before crossing boundary).
4) Decision events emitted to tracing and audit log with correlation_id, account_id, and policy_snapshot.
5) Integration tests covering: allowlist override, denylist block, EU-capacity exhaustion with ModelVariantFallback, and emergency_passthrough toggle.
6) Canary rollout plan defined in the playbook and validated in staging with SLO guardrails.
7) Documentation updated in Confluence with sample configs, JSON schema, and operator runbook.
tasks: Spec ResidenceChooser config schema and precedence rules (account > org > global)
Implement runtime adapter to query account residency metadata and capacity hints
Create allowlist/denylist storage and API (CRUD) with audit hooks
Add fallback selectors: ModelVariantFallback and TierFallback implementation
Wire decision events into tracing pipeline and audit log topic
Write integration tests and chaos test for EU capacity exhaustion
Author rollout playbook: canary gating, kill-switch, and post-mortem checklist
Confluence doc: operator runbook and sample JSON configs
Coordinate security review and update policy taxonomy
comments: 2025-02-11: Initial spec posted. Decided to keep precedence simple: explicit allowlist overrides > account residency flag > org default > global default. Avoiding per-route policy at first iteration for scope control. - A.P.

2025-02-17: Architecture review notes: Leah Chen recommended emitting full policy_snapshot in audit events to simplify future compliance audits; agreed to cap snapshot size by hashing large arrays. Action: Marco to add hash field. - Architecture

2025-02-21: Safety discussion: trade-off between StrictReject and availability. Proposed default to ModelVariantFallback (same jurisdiction variants) and reserve StrictReject for accounts who opt-in. PM requests UI hook to toggle emergency_passthrough. - Product
2025-02-28: Infra flagged potential capacity signal latency when querying Dedicated pool hints. Decided to introduce cached capacity hints with 30s TTL and health staleness metric. - Infra
2025-03-03: PR #4826 opened for ResidenceChooser core logic. Integration test harness added in ENG-764822. Need security review for allowlist CRUD endpoints (SAML roles + audit). - M.V.
2025-03-04: QA plan reviewed. Added chaos test to simulate EU pool outage and verify correct audit events and SLO alarms fire. - QA
